verses.text: [“]Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?

xrefs.text: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.
I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
And by that same word, the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
Extend Your loving devotion to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.

verses.text: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.

xrefs.text: You must not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which was set up by your ancestors to mark the inheritance you shall receive in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
‘Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.
The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.

verses.text: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

xrefs.text: Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security.
Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security.
When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security.
If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,

Here I am. Bear witness against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated or oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe and closed my eyes? Tell me, and I will restore it to you.”

verses.text: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

xrefs.text: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.
They trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth; they push the needy out of their way. A man and his father have relations with the same girl and so profane My holy name.
The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy and have exploited the foreign resident without justice.
Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.

verses.text: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.

xrefs.text: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil on their beds! At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.
The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
Man goes forth to his work and to his labor until evening.
Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.

verses.text: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.

xrefs.text: You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink the wine.
Whenever the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east would come up and invade them,
A people you do not know will eat the produce of your land and of all your toil. All your days you will be oppressed and crushed.

They will eat the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain or new wine or oil, no calves of your herds or lambs of your flocks, until they have caused you to perish.

verses.text: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.

xrefs.text: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you.
As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.
if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,

verses.text: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.

xrefs.text: Those who once ate delicacies are destitute in the streets; those brought up in crimson huddle in ash heaps.
The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.
I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”

verses.text: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.

xrefs.text: We and our children are just like our countrymen and their children, yet we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved, but we are powerless to redeem them because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”

Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”

verses.text: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

xrefs.text: They trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth; they push the needy out of their way. A man and his father have relations with the same girl and so profane My holy name.

If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.

verses.text: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.

xrefs.text: “Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness, and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his countrymen serve without pay, and fails to pay their wages,
Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

verses.text: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.

xrefs.text: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
So now we call the arrogant blessed. Not only do evildoers prosper, they even test God and escape.’”
You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.

verses.text: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.

xrefs.text: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.
But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.
And the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling— these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.
and with every wicked deception directed against those who are perishing, because they refused the love of the truth that would have saved them.

If indeed they have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again, their final condition is worse than it was at first.

verses.text: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.

xrefs.text: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil on their beds! At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.
For you are fully aware that the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
He lies in wait near the villages; in ambush he slays the innocent; his eyes watch in stealth for the helpless.
Remember, then, what you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know the hour when I will come upon you.
But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

verses.text: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.

xrefs.text: He says to himself, “God has forgotten; He hides His face and never sees.”
at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.
He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.

He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.’
They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob pays no heed.”

verses.text: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.

xrefs.text: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.
Have no fellowship with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them.
As they watch, dig through the wall and carry your belongings out through it.
If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,

verses.text: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!

xrefs.text: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
As the thief is ashamed when he is caught, so the house of Israel is disgraced. They, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets
And they said to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb.
Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.

verses.text: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.

xrefs.text: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country.
Cultivate your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer a harbor.
Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.

verses.text: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.

xrefs.text: Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?

verses.text: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.

xrefs.text: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
He called out in a loud voice: ‘Cut down the tree and chop off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.
The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’

verses.text: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.

xrefs.text: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her viciously to taunt her.
If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

verses.text: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.

xrefs.text: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.

Then Haman informed King Xerxes, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples of every province of your kingdom. Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws. So it is not in the king’s best interest to tolerate them.
From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.
And I saw three unclean spirits that looked like frogs coming out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.
The kings of the earth were immoral with her, and those who dwell on the earth were intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.

verses.text: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.

xrefs.text: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
While people are saying, “Peace and security, destruction will come upon them suddenly, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
Then I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am the One who searches minds and hearts, and I will repay each of you according to your deeds.
The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure— those who carry their god in their hands.
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.

verses.text: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

xrefs.text: Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found.
Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
that though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they will be forever destroyed.
I have seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree,
For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

verses.text: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”

xrefs.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
“Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?
But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
“Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
